Jesus wept. Let us look a moment at the character of Jesus: who, and what is he? If we accept the truths of the Bible, he is the son of God, The King of the Jews, The bright and morning star! A ruler of the Jews came to Jesus and said, "we know thou art a teacher come from God for no man can do the miracles that thou doest, except God be with him." We stand in awe as we contemplate them, and our hearts acknowledge him as King of Kings and Lord of Lords. But while we contemplate all of this glorious majesty our eye falls upon this simple sentence Jesus wept. What do we learn by this? by these two short words. We learn that He had a heart that could be touched by the sorrows and Suffering of our frail humanity: that Sympath[[lost: torn edge]]

[[Yellow?]] Branch [[illegible]]
Sept 18th 1863

Cousin George. I have written Several times to you but Silence has been the result. My uncertain Whereabouts perhaps have been the Cause — for I cannot think you so ungenerous as not to have Written to me Since Sept last year. I have thought my letters of last Spring may have Contained something not acceptable — if so I cannot conceive what it was — for if you are like the majority of Soldiers — your Feelings could hardly be ruffled — I will try you another Effort and if Silence is the response I may know Something is wrong in [[Denmark?]], & will call off my hounds. But as I am floating in rather a dull atmosphere I will not promise to be very interesting but trust I may for a while relieve you of the monotony of the Camps.

I am home on a detail after Clothing for our Co. having reached Sat Evening. I find things moving on in this vicinity about like they did before the War began save the absence of Young men. Plenty Seems Smiling at every door — and were it not for absent ones I believe the people here would be happy. [[illegible]] quite warm weathering Carried on in North Carolina. As yet I have visited but Little. I have visited Waxahachie twice — a very important case being under Consideration in the Court — To wit; The murder of a Mrs Claunch by her Daughter — The case has not yet been decided but from the evidence I have heard believe she will come clear — but not in the Eyes of the people — as innocent of the offence. From Waxa on Monday I went to Red Oak Camp Ground — Camp meeting being on hand — and have remained till Tuesday — The meeting not so largely attended as in former years — Especially by the Sterner Sex — but there has been no discount on the other Side. The eating part received marked attention on my part. I indulge freely in those Substantials that keep Soul & body together — but did not Labor very hard to make myself agreeable — or to create a Contagious Sometimes Called a “palpitation of the heart” — My observation teaches me That the germs of this malady are in an [[illegible]] State and only need Sunshine to bring them to bloom, Expand & Captivate —

They had Shouting times that night — Some things done rather disorders — Some Singular movements. Amongst them was a Soldier friend — who yielded to the Solicitation of an Old Gentleman who has a Daughter that has [[illegible]] Claims upon him — I think the meeting is Still in operation — If Shoutings are an indication of Godliness — This is Certainly the most Christian people in the range of my knowledge. Possibly this may be attributable to the fact of the abundance of Preachers — who Claim exemption by reason of their vocation and fearing if they do not all Preach they will have to Shoulder their musket & Battle Some

Some other time. I spent the time very pleasantly & only Regreted that I Couldent Stay longer I Shall never forget the kind people of Ala.
At the expiration of my furlough I Started [[lost: reproduced portion ends]]

I Remain as ever your true Brother
James [[illegible]]

Palestine, Sept. 8th 1851
Dear Father,
Your letter of August 16th came to hand a few days ago, and I was much gratified to hear from you all again. I have just been writing to sister Rebecca, and scolded a good deal with [[her?]] for none of you writing to me, but I see from your letter that the fault lay entirely with the mail, so I shall not send it. I am glad to hear of the good health of the Family, and it gives me some hopes that health may be enjoyed in [[Burky?]], as well as other places. This County although reputed to be one of the healthiest in the State, has been very sickly for two months past, more so than I ever saw it in Ellis Co. I think that Old Mr Benson is nearly willing to try the [[illegible]] again for he has not bettered himself so far as health is concerned, by moving down here.
There has been a great many deaths in the county, & five Doctors living in this place have had their hands full of practice, tho' now it is becoming [[margin]] more healthy [[/margin]]

My own health never was better than it has been since I have been in this place. I still get plenty of work to do. I quit working for Mr Dale about a month ago & have been picking up little jobs round ever since. Were it not so expensive to live here I could make a tolerably fair living. I am now helping [[Hedlie?]] a large Livery Stable, my wages are $1,50 cts pr day, but after subtracting $10 pr month for board & washing, the amount is considerably diminished.
There is going to be a very good opening for carpenters here this coming Winter and Spring, and I am somewhat at a loss whether to continue journeywork or turn out undertaker, I think I could get plenty to do either way.
The Christian Church at this place have resolved to build a house of worship as soon as lumber can be procured. It will be 56 ft long & 34 wide and will present a very neat appearance when finished. It has not rained here for so long that I forget when it did rain last, every thing is very much parched up. Corn crops are tolerably good, but Cotton will not make more than a half crop

There in mist my vision failing
As bending o’er the iron railing
Vain regrets my soul assailing
Passed in review a life that little fruitage bore.
All its longing and its yearning
All its fruits to ashes turning
All its fever fiercely burning
Through my frenzied brain, the stormy passions tore

The years to come all desolated
To the thorn and rockwaste fated
Dull despair to sorrow mated
Spread their pall upon the soul and bid hope [[flee?]] [[door?]]
Clouds above—the darkness falling
Night’s deep’ning gloom in mist appalling
Future years to conflict calling
Conflict with that Fate which life’s disasters bore

Yesterday brought its roseate vision
Today Fate holds us in derision
Tomorrow in the fields elysian
We’ll dream again the dreams dreamed on life’s
Sunrise shore

Jesus wept. Let us look a moment at the character of Jesus: who, and what is he? If we accept the truths of the Bible, he is the son of God, The King of the Jews, The bright and morning star! By His word the tempest is stilled, and He walks the waves of the wild Galilee. By His word the dead are called back to life again. Truly He was the son of God.

Renan in his Life of Christ says "All ages will proclaim that among the sons of men there were none born greater than Jesus." His goodness, [[greatness?]], his omnipotent power, we cannot doubt. We stand in awe as we contemplate them, and our hearts acknowledge him as King of Kings and Lord of Lords. We know not, but this is the beginning of terrible times. I hate the thought that Brushy [[deleted: should]] should be the place of the beginning of such things. I would feel a great deal better if I knew that man was not hanging over in that thicket.

Ann & Cynthia have just passed by going from aunt Catherines and say Warren Payne is dying he has been sick for some time. Lizzie and I will go up to sit up to night.

Warren Payne is the youngest child of Preston Payne whom aunt [[inserted: Catherine]] took when he was only nine days old and has kept him ever since. Had he have lived seven more days he would be seventeen months old. His disease was chronic diarhea. Lynn Norman is at home on furlough; he has been out on the RioGrande for some months but is on his way to La. He has to report at Sabinetown on the eighth of Sept. He says the Reg. to which Eppa belongs has been ordered to Arizona. Another wildgoose chase like that of Sibleys Brigade. Gran Jetter is still at home. I dont think he is in much of a hurry to return to his command as he has been digging a well for two or three weeks past and intends to finish dig and [[wole?]] it with white rock before he thinks about fixing to go back. His furlough has been out a long time and he says when he is in the army all he thinks about is how to manage to get another. His patriotism has cooled down several degrees below zero. Mr. Chappell and his son Bob were in fifty miles of their home the last that has been heard of them. They are now violent secesh, but doubtless have got home and taken the oath to the feds long ago to keep out of the service in Dixie. Miss Ada Chappell is living at Gran Jettons and she is so patriotic that she says she had rather her father and brothers would all be killed than for this confederacy to go down. but she knows they are all out of danger now for Dock deserted and went home from La. last fall you can now form some idea of what kind of folks they are.
Sue
